PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior. RATIONALE: Single responsibility helps pinpoint failures. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test tests exactly one behavior and has one Arrange-Act-Assert. DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations: the method contains a single operation (constructor call). 2) Name does not suggest multiple operations. 3) Single operation and no assertions but single Arrange-Act (construction) -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method contains exactly one action (new MaxMin4()) and does not perform multiple independent operations.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent. RATIONALE: Independence enables reordering and parallel runs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if setup/teardown used or tests use only local variables. DECISION RULES: 1) No @Before/@After annotations found in method scope. 2) No static/instance mutable state is used in the method: it only uses a local variable. 3) No ordered naming. 4) Tests use only local variables -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant because this method uses only local variables and does not rely on external/shared mutable state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover happy and error paths. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when there are at least two tests per method (happy + error) or tests explicitly check exceptions. DECISION RULES: 1) Count test methods in the class: only one test method exists. 2) No @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows present. 3) No method names indicating error tests. 4) Since the class has <2 test methods and no exception testing, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because only a single, happy-path-style constructor call exists and there are no tests exercising error/exceptional flows.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should check boundary values. RATIONALE: Boundaries reveal off-by-one and range errors. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests include empty strings, zero, negatives, max/min, or names indicate boundary testing. DECISION RULES: 1) No boundary-like test data is present. 2) No method names indicate boundary/edge testing. 3) The test uses only a constructor call with no inputs to check boundaries. 4) Because the test supplies only a typical (no-arg) construction and no boundary data, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there are no boundary checks or inputs exercising edge conditions.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants exist or if tests are so small they don't repeat. DECISION RULES: 1) No helper methods present, 2) No constants present, 3) Tests are very short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code -> mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test is very short and does not duplicate code across methods (only one method present), so modularity concerns are minimal.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to reason about. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test performs only construction and has no assertions that verify object state or behavior.
